content.text: What is the desired outcome of this ticket? to document the change in behavior or to return to the previous 404 behavior?
Unless there is a specific reason for the change, I think we should revert to the old behavior.
And just to make sure we're on the same page here — I think both this change and
are very minor, unintentional changes, but that they are nonetheless breaking changes, so they shouldn't be included in 4.7.1.
, the description in this ticket mentions getting a 404 with Fedora 4.7.0. But your example shows getting a 400 with both Fedora 4.7.0 and 4.7.1-RC... which is what I am seeing as well.
Can you verify which version of Fedora responds with a 404?

, I would swear I was seeing a 404 before, but I am now testing with various older versions of Fedora and seeing a 400 Bad Request response in all of them.  It's possible that there was a change in client behavior or something else that caused the test failures I was seeing (
https://gist.github.com/escowles/50eaf62b45e3de313622dcef705496bf)
Since you -
- may return to this, I reran my quick tests.  All against tomcat7 and postgres9.4:

# FCREPO 4.6.0
curl -I http://192.168.99.100:8080/fcrepo/rest/invalid:foo
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 38
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2017 17:01:01 GMT
Connection: close

# FCREPO 4.6.1
curl -I http://192.168.99.100:8080/fcrepo/rest/invalid:foo
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 38
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2017 17:05:30 GMT
Connection: close

# FCREPO 4.7.0
curl -I http://192.168.99.100:8080/fcrepo/rest/invalid:foo
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 38
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2017 17:08:56 GMT
Connection: close

# FCREPO 4.7.1-rc1
curl -I http://192.168.99.100:8080/fcrepo/rest/invalid:foo
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 38
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2017 17:10:29 GMT
Connection: close
I think the key issue here is that invalid namespace handling hasn't change — but the test: namespace used to be registered, but was removed between 4.7.0 and 4.7.1-RC-1:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/48010a20a13645977d4641cb987c939f6e2522b8#diff-f793c1dd76ef43f9673963a55a86fd8cL37
Can we reinstate the test namespace prefix, and remove it in a later major release?
I'm a little confused - what is the relationship between performing a HEAD on
http://192.168.99.100:8080/fcrepo/rest/invalid:foo
and the absence of registered test: prefix?
— the ActiveFedora test that led to this issue was doing a HEAD on the URL
http://localhost:8986/rest/test/test:123
.  In 4.7.0, that returns a 404 (because the test: prefix is registered), but in 4.7.1-RC-1, it returns a 410 (because test: was removed).
I incorrectly thought it was the namespace handling that had changed.  But in fact, it was the removal of the test: prefix that caused the change in behavior.
OK, so with 4.7.0, I get:
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test:123
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/TEST:123
So with 4.7.1-RC, I get:
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test:123
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/TEST:123
Would the correct behavior be:
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/test:123
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/TEST:123
(since both URIs don't actually resolve to a web resource that exists)?
, I think 4.7.1 should have the same behavior as 4.7.0.  After that, I'm fine with removing the test: prefix so that we'd return 400 for anything that used it.
I think there may be two issues here:
1) the removal of "test:" prefix in the cnd file.  This has implications beyond the 400/404 issue, so it makes sense to keep "test:" around for the 4.7.x series in its own right
2) Fedora's response code to URIs that look like
http://path/to/resource/prefix:whatever

. Should the http response codes be affected by the contents of the cnd file at all?  Shouldn't they just be 404s (resource does not exist) rather than 400 (you're not interacting with this resource correctly)?
+1 to retaining the current behavior in 4.7.x
As for '2', I don't see why it should be affected by the 'cnd' file unless the cnd file defines that specific node (not the namespace), such that it
should
exist.  It seems to me that, if, for example,
http://192.168.99.100:8080/fcrepo/rest/invalid:foo

doesn't exist, then it should return a 404.  If, however, it does exist - or it is a service that should exist - and you are interacting with it incorrectly, it would be a 400 (or Bad Request) or possibly a 405 (depending).
Agreed.  It seems that addressing (1) by adding back the test namespace to the cnd file will restore the 4.7.0 behavior described in this ticket.

I think that (2) should probably be a separate ticket, and should not be considered a blocker for 4.7.1.  If the end solution is 404s universally, then that shouldn't break Hydra tests as it's looking for a 404 anyway
By the way, just out of curiosity, why is ActiveFedora making requests to a URI like
http://localhost:8986/rest/test/test:123
in the first place?  Are the tests intentionally trying to provoke a 404 from Fedora by using a random URI that shouldn't exist?
? Would one of you be interested in submitting a PR?
I've put in a PR to restore the test namespace:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1153

, yes, that's it exactly.  The test in question was doing head and get requests for objects it expected not to exist, to make sure it got the correct error from the LDP client in that situation.  I think the test: prefix was a holdover from Fedora 3 days, and happened to keep working because it was also defined in the CND file.
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/6a0bcda5ed1d3fc93375302091aa20fe80b7bfc3
With Fedora 4.7.0, when I do a HEAD request on a non-existent repository URI with an invalid namespace, I get a 404:
$ curl -I
http://localhost:8080/rest/invalid:foo
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Date: Thu, 22 Dec 2016 19:14:39 GMT
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 38
Server: Jetty(9.2.3.v20140905)
(An error about the invalid namespace prefix is logged to the server log, but not displayed to the user in any way).
With 4.7.1-RC-1, I get a 400 Bad Request:
$ curl -I
http://localhost:8080/rest/invalid:foo
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Date: Thu, 22 Dec 2016 19:15:53 GMT
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 38
Server: Jetty(9.2.3.v20140905)
